entity.summary: LLCs and corporations are formed with the Department of Financial Institutions; Wisconsin's One Stop Business Registration lets you register with DFI, Revenue and Workforce Development together.
entity.quote: One Stop Business Registration to register your business with multiple agencies, including the Department of Financial Institutions and the Department of Workforce Development.

state_tax.summary: Register with the Department of Revenue for sales tax and withholding permits, either directly or through One Stop Business Registration.
state_tax.quote: Register with Department of Revenue if any of the following apply

unemployment.agency: WI Department of Workforce Development, Unemployment Insurance Division
unemployment.summary: You become a covered employer for unemployment insurance if you pay $1,500 or more in wages in a quarter, or employ someone in 20 or more weeks in a year.
unemployment.quote: You paid wages of $1,500 or more in a quarter in any calendar year or; ... You employed one or more individuals in employment for some part of a day in 20 or more weeks in any calendar year.

workers_comp.agency: WI Department of Workforce Development, Worker's Compensation Division
workers_comp.summary: You must carry workers' comp (from a private insurer) once you employ 3 or more people, or pay $500 or more in wages in a quarter to 1 or more employees. Small closely held corporations with no more than two officers and no other employees can opt out.
workers_comp.quote: Employ 3 or more full-time or part-time employees. ... Pay gross wages of $500 or more in any quarter for 1 or more employees for work done in Wisconsin.

residential_building.name: Dwelling Contractor certification (business) and Dwelling Contractor Qualifier certification (individual)
residential_building.agency: WI Department of Safety and Professional Services (DSPS)
residential_building.covers: Contractors who obtain building permits for one- and two-family dwellings (new homes, additions, remodels needing a permit).
prerequisites: Dwelling Contractor Qualifier (owner or employee) completes at least 12 hours in an approved qualifier course
Surety bond of at least $25,000 (proof of financial responsibility)
General liability insurance of at least $250,000 per occurrence
Attest compliance with workers' comp and unemployment requirements
residential_building.insurance: General liability insurance of at least $250,000 per occurrence.
residential_building.summary: To pull building permits on one- and two-family homes in Wisconsin, your business needs a Dwelling Contractor certification and must hold or employ a certified Dwelling Contractor Qualifier, who completes a 12-hour course. The business must show a bond and liability insurance.
residential_building.quote: no person may obtain a building permit for a one and two family dwelling unless the person compiles with the following

evidence.quote: Holds a Dwelling contractor certification or a Dwelling Contractor Restricted Certification issued by the Department.
Complete at least 12 hours in an approved initial qualifier course in dwelling construction.
A copy of a bond of at least $25,000 endorsed by a surety company authorized to do business in Wisconsin.
A certificate of general liability insurance of at least $250,000 per occurrence.
By submitting this application the applicant is attesting that the business is in compliance with worker's compensation requirements and unemployment compensation requirements

commercial_building.agency: WI Department of Safety and Professional Services
commercial_building.covers: The Dwelling Contractor credential applies to one- and two-family dwelling permits; there is no general state commercial contractor license.
commercial_building.summary: Wisconsin has no statewide general contractor license for commercial work; the Dwelling Contractor certification is tied to permits for one- and two-family homes. Trade credentials (electrical, plumbing, HVAC) still apply.
commercial_building.quote: For the owner, partner, or chief executive of a contracting business seeking certification to obtain building permits for one- and two-family dwellings for the first time.
commercial_building.note: No DSPS page found stating outright that commercial general contractors are unlicensed; inferred from the dwelling-only scope.

electrical.name: Electrical Contractor license (business); Master and Journeyman Electrician licenses (individual)
electrical.agency: WI Department of Safety and Professional Services
electrical.covers: Electrical contracting businesses and individual electricians.
prerequisites: Journeyman: a 3-year approved electrician apprenticeship, or 48 months and 8,000 hours of experience, then pass the exam
Master: twelve months as a licensed journeyman (or 60 months with 10,000 hours, or an electrical engineering degree), then pass the exam
Electrical contractor: applied for by the owner, partner or CEO (no exam)
electrical.summary: Wisconsin licenses electrical contracting businesses and individual electricians through DSPS. Journeymen qualify through a 3-year apprenticeship or 8,000 hours of experience; masters need twelve months as a licensed journeyman. Both must pass an exam.
electrical.quote: Completion of a construction electrician apprenticeship program in installing, repairing, and maintaining electrical wiring that has a duration of at least 3 years

evidence.quote: Experience in installing, repairing, and maintaining electrical wiring during a period of not less than 48 months, with at least 8,000 hours of experience over that period.
Twelve months of experience in installing, repairing, and maintaining electrical wiring while being licensed as a Journeyman Electrician
Experience in installing, repairing, and maintaining electrical wiring during a period of not less than 60 months, with at least 10,000 hours of experience over that period
The person applying for an electrical contractor license shall be one of the following:

electrical.note: Statute requiring an electrical contractor to employ a master electrician (Wis. Stat. 101.862) could not be fetched; not stated here.

plumbing.name: Master Plumber and Journeyman Plumber licenses (plus restricted service/appliance licenses)
plumbing.agency: WI Department of Safety and Professional Services
plumbing.covers: Individual plumbers; plumbing work is done under licensed master plumbers.
prerequisites: Journeyman: complete a recognized plumbing apprenticeship program, then pass the exam
Master: at least 1,000 hours per year for at least 3 years as a Wisconsin licensed journeyman (or an engineering degree), then pass the exam
plumbing.summary: Wisconsin licenses plumbers through DSPS. Journeymen must finish a recognized apprenticeship and pass an exam; masters need 3 years as a licensed journeyman (1,000 hours a year) and another exam.
plumbing.quote: A person applying for a Journeyman Plumber license examination shall have completed a plumbing apprenticeship program recognized under Wisconsin Statute chapter 106 or the Federal Department of Labor

evidence.quote: At least 1,000 hours of plumbing related work experience per year for at least 3 years as a Wisconsin licensed journeyman plumber

mechanical.name: HVAC Contractor registration (business) and HVAC Qualifier certification (individual)
mechanical.agency: WI Department of Safety and Professional Services
mechanical.covers: HVAC contracting businesses register with DSPS; the HVAC Qualifier is an individual exam-based credential.
prerequisites: HVAC Contractor registration applied for by the owner, partner or CEO
HVAC Qualifier exam: at least 1000 hours per year for at least 4 years of HVAC experience, or 4 years of HVAC-related schooling, or a combination
mechanical.summary: HVAC businesses register with DSPS as HVAC Contractors. The HVAC Qualifier credential requires about 4 years of HVAC experience or schooling and an exam.
mechanical.quote: The person applying for a HVAC Contractor registration shall be one of the following:

evidence.quote: At least 1000 hours per year for at least 4 years of experience in supervising or performing the design, installation, servicing or maintenance of HVAC systems or equipment

mechanical.note: Whether an HVAC contractor must employ an HVAC Qualifier is set in SPS 305; not quoted here.

roofing.agency: WI Department of Safety and Professional Services
roofing.covers: No separate roofing license; roofers pulling permits on one- and two-family dwellings need the Dwelling Contractor certification.
roofing.summary: Wisconsin has no separate roofing license. If a roofing job on a one- or two-family home needs a building permit, the contractor pulling it must hold the Dwelling Contractor certification and employ a Dwelling Contractor Qualifier.
roofing.quote: no person may obtain a building permit for a one and two family dwelling unless the person compiles with the following
roofing.note: Roofing is not listed among DSPS trade credentials.

pesticide.name: Commercial Pesticide Applicator certification and license; Pesticide Business License
pesticide.agency: WI Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection (DATCP)
pesticide.covers: For-hire pesticide applicators (pest control, lawn care, tree spraying) and the businesses employing them.
prerequisites: Work for or obtain a Pesticide Business License
pesticide.summary: For-hire applicators need certification (by exam), an individual commercial applicator license, and must work for a business holding a Pesticide Business License. Businesses must employ certified and licensed applicators.
pesticide.quote: For-hire applicators need three things before making a commercial application:

evidence.quote: Work for or obtain a Pesticide Business License (PBL) (this gets renewed annually, January 1-December 31).

asbestos.name: Asbestos company and individual certification
asbestos.agency: WI Department of Health Services, Asbestos Program
asbestos.covers: Persons and companies doing regulated asbestos work during renovation or demolition.
prerequisites: DHS asbestos training and certification for workers and the company
asbestos.summary: Wisconsin DHS certifies people and companies that do regulated asbestos work, such as abatement during renovation or demolition.
asbestos.quote: helps protect people from exposure to asbestos from building renovations and demolitions by ensuring proper training and certification for persons and companies conducting regulated asbestos work.

lead_rrp.name: Lead Company certification and Lead-Safe Renovator certification
lead_rrp.agency: WI Department of Health Services, Lead-Safe Wisconsin
lead_rrp.covers: Renovation that disturbs paint in houses and child care centers built before 1978.
prerequisites: Certify your company with DHS (sole proprietors certify under a company name)
Individual lead-safe renovator training and certification
lead_rrp.summary: Wisconsin runs its own lead-safe renovation program instead of EPA. Both your company and the individual renovator must be certified by DHS to do paint-disturbing work in pre-1978 homes and child care centers.
lead_rrp.quote: You must go through training and get certified to work with lead-based paint in houses and child care centers built before 1978. Both individual and company certification are needed.

evidence.quote: These states are authorized to administer their own RRP programs in lieu of the federal program.

other.name: Automatic Fire Sprinkler Contractor and Fitter licenses
other.agency: WI Department of Safety and Professional Services
other.summary: DSPS credentials fire sprinkler contractors, fitters and testers.
